questions.question: Explain the concept of novelty in patenting biotech inventions.
questions.solution_html:
• The invention must be new and not previously known or disclosed anywhere in the world
  • before the patent application is filed. The concept of novelty is one of the key requirements
  • for granting a patent in biotechnology and other fields. It ensures that only truly new and
  • original inventions receive protection. In biotechnology, novelty means that the invention—
  • such as a new gene sequence, microorganism, genetically modified plant, or process— has not
  • been made public anywhere in the world before the date of the patent application.
questions.final_answer: been made public anywhere in the world before the date of the patent application

questions.question: Define trademark infringement and explain its essential features.
questions.solution_html:
• Trademark infringement is the unauthorized use of a registered trademark or a deceptively similar
  • mark by another party, in a way that is likely to cause confusion, deception, or misunderstanding
  • among consumers about the origin of goods or services.
  • • Unauthorized use: The trademark is used without the permission of the registered owner.
  • • Identical or deceptively similar mark: The infringing mark closely resembles the registered
  • one in appearance, sound, or meaning.
questions.final_answer: one in appearance, sound, or meaning
